text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- President Jacques Chirac in television interview last night reaffirmed his electoral committments to reducing gap between the poor and wealthy, and sought to explain need for austerity policy and cuts in public deficits. He said a european single currency was necessary to fend off the dollar's monetary hegemony. A devaluation of the franc against the mark would hurt Europe and prove useless, and concluded by ruling out a cabinet reshuffle. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- France Telecom state-owned operator announces price cuts in domestic and international communications, and a hike in monthly subscription rates, ahead of a 1998 European telecommunications deregulation.
-- State to sell its stake in defence electronics unit Thomson-CSF in Thomson SA privatisation in early 1997, postpones privatisation of consumer electronics arm Thomson Multimedia.
-- Unions and management at Credit Lyonnais reach agreement on shorter work week to avoid part of planned job cuts linked to restructuring.
-- Groupe Bollore executive Vincent Parayre says it may join British Airways in possible attempt to buy domestic airline AOM.
-- Bouygues confirms buying 80 percent of water supply unit Cise from Saint-Gobain for 2.16 billion francs.
-- French and German heads of state vow to reach agreement on "monetary stability pact" at Dublin European summit today and tomorrow.
-- Rhone-Poulenc enters capital of CFPI agro-chemical firm and proposes joint-venture on three products.
-- Bouygues to restructure its capital along with a planned merger of water supplier Saur with Saint-Gobain's Cise, would eventually own 83 percent of the merged company.

-- Thomson Multimedia chairman Alain Prestat confirmed in job, will tackle restructuring and aim for a return to balance before a privatisation, helped by a planned 10-billion-francs recapitalisation expected before end April 1997.
-- Acquisition by Carrefour of stake in Groupe GMB which controls hypermarkets Cora fans speculation about consolidation in the French retail sector.
